subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?
questions.explain: Coal, along with oil and natural gas, is a fossil fuel formed from the remains of ancient organisms.

questions.q: Which statement best describes fossil fuels?
options: They can be replaced within a human lifetime
questions.explain: Fossil fuels exist in limited quantities and cannot be replenished on a human timescale, making them non-renewable.

questions.q: Which raw material is used to fuel a nuclear power station?
questions.explain: Nuclear power stations use uranium as fuel, releasing energy through nuclear fission.

questions.q: What is the main environmental problem caused by burning fossil fuels?
options: Release of carbon dioxide, contributing to global warming
Depletion of the ozone layer only
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming.

questions.q: What is one advantage of nuclear power compared with burning fossil fuels?
options: It produces no carbon dioxide during electricity generation
It uses a renewable fuel source
It produces no waste at all
It is completely free of any hazard
questions.explain: Nuclear power generates electricity without releasing carbon dioxide, unlike fossil fuel combustion.

questions.q: Which group correctly lists three fossil fuels?
questions.explain: The three main fossil fuels are coal, oil (petroleum) and natural gas.

questions.q: What is a major disadvantage of nuclear power?
options: It produces radioactive waste that is difficult to dispose of
It releases large amounts of carbon dioxide
It relies on sunlight to operate
The fuel is regrown each year
questions.explain: Nuclear power creates radioactive waste that remains hazardous for a long time and is difficult to store safely.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Solar energy is renewable because sunlight is continually available and not depleted by use.

questions.q: Which device converts sunlight directly into electricity?
questions.explain: Photovoltaic cells convert light energy from the Sun directly into electrical energy.

questions.q: How does a wind turbine generate electricity?
options: Moving air turns blades that drive a generator
Sunlight heats water to make steam
questions.explain: The kinetic energy of moving air turns the turbine blades, which rotate a generator to produce electricity.

questions.q: A village beside a fast-flowing river with a dam wants a reliable, continuous supply of renewable electricity. Which source is most suitable?
questions.explain: Hydroelectric power uses flowing or falling water to drive turbines, giving a reliable renewable supply where a dam and river are available.

questions.q: Why are solar and wind power described as intermittent?
options: They are not always available, depending on weather and time of day
questions.explain: Solar power needs daylight and wind power needs wind, so their output is intermittent rather than constant.

questions.q: Geothermal energy is obtained from which source?
questions.explain: Geothermal energy uses heat stored beneath the Earth's surface to generate electricity or provide heating.

questions.q: Why is biomass considered a renewable energy source?
options: The plants and crops used as fuel can be regrown
It produces no waste of any kind
The fuel is mined from underground
questions.explain: Biomass fuels come from plants and organic material that can be replanted and regrown, making the source renewable.

questions.q: A remote off-grid cabin on an exposed, consistently windy coastal cliff needs its own electricity supply. Which renewable source best suits this location?
questions.explain: A consistently windy exposed site makes a wind turbine the most practical renewable choice for local generation.

questions.q: Why are several cells often connected together to form a battery?
options: To provide a higher voltage or greater capacity than a single cell
To make the product heavier on purpose
To remove the need for any circuit
questions.explain: Connecting cells together in a battery increases the available voltage and/or capacity beyond that of one cell.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an alkaline battery and a rechargeable battery?
options: Alkaline batteries are single-use, whereas rechargeable batteries can be reused many times
Alkaline batteries store more energy and last forever
Rechargeable batteries can never be reused
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: Alkaline cells are non-rechargeable and discarded once flat, while rechargeable cells can be recharged and reused repeatedly.

questions.q: Which type of rechargeable battery is commonly used in mobile phones and laptops?
questions.explain: Lithium-ion rechargeable batteries are widely used in phones and laptops because they are lightweight with a high energy capacity.

questions.q: A games controller is used every day and would otherwise need new batteries very frequently. Why would rechargeable batteries be the better design choice?
options: They reduce ongoing cost and waste from constantly replacing single-use cells
They release carbon dioxide as they discharge
They can only ever be used once
questions.explain: For frequently used products, rechargeable batteries cut long-term cost and reduce the waste created by disposing of single-use cells.

questions.q: A designer needs a lightweight, high-capacity, rechargeable power source for a slim portable product. Which battery type is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Lithium-ion batteries offer a high energy capacity for their light weight and are rechargeable, suiting slim portable products.
